bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in US tariff refund accounting; Geopolitical disruption in Middle East shipping routes; Raw material volatility (PTA/MEG); Execution risk on 50-studio D2C rollout.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and aggressive on volume growth; Disciplined on capital allocation; Transparent on tariff headwinds; Bullish on D2C margin expansion.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Sun-control line expansion prioritized over PPF due to higher fungibility (can produce PPF if needed) and larger absolute capacity addition (125 lakh sq ft/month vs 25 lakh for PPF); Architectural films growing faster than automotive due to 'privacy on demand' (PDLC) adoption.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "₹ 774 crores liquidity surplus (as on 31st March 2026)"; cash, bank & liquid funds series shown as 308 / 387 / 388 / 650 / 774 for FY22-FY26.
- "Healthy Cash flows Net Zero debt"; the gross debt series is shown as 182 / 141 / 0 / 0 / 0 across FY22-FY26, with a footnote "**Debt repayment of ₹ 141 cr in FY24".
- "Regular Dividend paying company" (no payout ratio or dividend amount is disclosed in the deck).
- Fixed-asset turnover is presented on two bases — "Adj Fixed Assets Turnover*" and "Fixed Assets Turnover ratio" — with the footnote "*Adjusted for Revaluation reserve of ₹ 764 Cr".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Fully vertically integrated chips-to-film production — complete control from petrochemical intermediate to finished product eliminates dependency on other manufacturers and gives high control over quality and product range
- India's only manufacturer of Sun Control films and Paint Protection Films, and the only producer of professional-grade PPF in India
- Specialised products carry significant entry barriers due to stringent quality focus, proprietary composition and processes, and limited competition
- Value Added Products accounted for 87% of total revenue in FY2025-26, making earnings more predictable and gross margins steadier as the mix shifts away from commodity
- ~90% market share in India's shrink film segment
- Distribution reach: 250+ Garware Application Studios, 90+ countries served, and a top-exporter position won from PLEXCONCIL for 38 consecutive years
- DSIR-accredited in-house R&D centre with pilot-scale plants, a pioneer in BOPET, solar control, lidding and PPF product development
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Trade policy and tariff exposure on exports — Management calls trade policy the most acute challenge: phased US tariffs on Indian exports of up to 50% were a major headwind in FY2026, and Q2 FY2026 revenues were down ~8% YoY due to the high tariff situation in the USA. Mitigation via cost efficiencies, front-loading shipments and market diversification, but the uncertainty remains.
- Raw material price volatility linked to crude oil — The Company's major raw materials, PTA and MEG, are derived from crude oil, so crude price fluctuations directly impact raw material costs. Increases are passed on only to the extent feasible and required; commodity inflation in oil and energy also squeezed margins.
- Currency fluctuation on a heavily export-weighted revenue base — Given the Company's significant export revenues it is exposed to currency fluctuations. It appoints consultants who advise on global economic events and their impact on currencies, and hedges its net exposure through forward contracts.
- Competition risk from capacity additions by global and domestic film majors — The Company is sensitive to industry capacity, output levels, economic conditions and changes in consumer demand; the addition of capacities by competitors has intensified competition. Mitigated through product differentiation, market expansion and continuous market analysis.
- Operational risk from equipment obsolescence — Equipment obsolescence could disrupt production. The Company monitors equipment performance, conducts timely upgrades and preventive maintenance, and has made significant investments in equipment modernisation.
- Logistics and geopolitical disruption — Logistics risks encompass transportation challenges and the availability of shipping containers, with geopolitical challenges from the Middle East and Eastern Europe; the Directors' Report also cites the impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict alongside U.S. tariff uncertainty.
- End-market cyclicality and demand concentration in automotive and real estate — In domestic markets, timely project execution such as new real-estate projects can be cyclical, and any slowdown in key end-user sectors (automotive, real estate) would impact volumes.
- Broad enterprise risk set flagged by the Board — The Company's ERM exercise identifies changing regulations, intensifying competition, business uncertainties, technological obsolescence, investment risks, financial challenges, environmental concerns and talent retention as key risks. The Board holds overall responsibility for the risk management framework, supported by a Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 of the Listing Regulations; in the Committee's and Board's opinion no risk threatens the existence of the Company.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: GHFL manufactures BOPET polyester films and value-added specialty films at a fully integrated chips-to-film plant, producing its own resins in-house before converting them into finished film. Its portfolio spans architectural (sun control) films, automotive sun control and safety glazing films, paint protection films, and industrial/value-added films for electrical & electronics, packaging, thermal, shrink label and lidding applications. The business is organised into a Consumer Product Division serving solar control, window lamination, architectural and paint protection end-uses, and an Industrial Product Division supplying converters serving food, pharmaceutical and personal care brands.

outlook.body:
- Expand and diversify the product portfolio toward specialty and novel products, led by the upcoming TPU product line
- Shift mix further toward Value Added Products, repurposing older lines for specialty film production to lift capacity utilisation and make earnings more predictable
- Diversify export markets away from US concentration — expansion into the Middle East via a planned Dubai subsidiary and a bolstered European team
- Build B2C reach internationally through Global Application Studios in the United States and the Middle East
- Launch a first-of-its-kind D2C business model in India through Garware Home Solutions, with strategic entry into the signage and digital printing segments
- Broaden the automotive offering with advanced detailing products including ceramic and graphene solutions
- Build direct digital channels (online sales, apps, digital marketing and channel-partner platforms) to enhance market access and brand loyalty
- Digital transformation of operations: advanced analytics for manufacturing and supply chain, ERP upgradation, cybersecurity hardening and IT infrastructure enhancement
- Sustain R&D-led differentiation through the DSIR-accredited R&D centre, launching coloured PPF, Headlight PPF, Spectrally Selective Films and Safety & Security Films

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: GHFL is setting up a TPU plant with a capacity of 360 LSF per annum, which was under progress at the end of FY2025-26, and commissioned its second Paint Protection Film line in the second quarter of FY2025-26. The Board approved on January 22, 2026 the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai, UAE, still in process of incorporation, as part of a Middle East expansion that alongside a bolstered European team is intended to diversify export markets away from US geopolitical risk. The Company operates 3 manufacturing sites and 3 offices nationally plus 2 international offices (US and UK, for its subsidiaries), and runs four manufacturing lines housing administrative, manufacturing and R&D functions; it continues to repurpose older lines for specialty film production, which management describes as a key driver of strong capacity utilisation. Channel and footprint expansion includes the launch of Global Application Studios in the United States and the Middle East, over 250 Garware Application Studios, a D2C model through Garware Home Solutions in India, and strategic entry into signage and digital printing. Significant investments have been made in equipment modernisation to ensure operational efficiency and minimise disruptions.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global push for energy efficiency and UV protection in buildings and vehicles underpins the Sun Control film business
- Growing luxury car and EV adoption supports the high-margin PPF segment
- Nascent 'smart glass' and architectural film markets offer high potential as commercial and residential developers seek modern solutions
- Trade policy is the most acute headwind — phased US tariffs on Indian exports of up to 50%, with Q2 FY2026 revenues down ~8% YoY on the tariff situation in the USA; mitigating actions taken were cost efficiencies, front-loading shipments and market diversification, but uncertainty remains
- Raw material volatility: PTA and MEG are crude-oil derived, so crude price moves feed directly into input costs; increases are passed on to the extent feasible
- Commodity inflation in oil and energy plus logistics costs squeezed margins
- Competitive pressure from global film majors continues, offset by GHFL's R&D and pricing flexibility
- Domestic project execution is cyclical, and a slowdown in key end-user sectors such as automotive and real estate would impact volumes
- Value Added Products reached 87% of total revenue in FY2025-26, reinforcing the transition toward high-value specialty businesses
- Despite uncertainty of U.S. tariff rates and the impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict, the Company was able to maintain profit levels broadly in line with the previous year

deepdive.thesis: Garware Hi-Tech delivered record Q4/FY26 profitability (EBITDA margin 26.2%) driven by operational leverage and product mix, while guiding for ~18% revenue growth in FY27 backed by a new INR191cr sun-control line and aggressive D2C studio expansion. The key catalyst remains the potential accounting benefit from US tariff refunds and imminent anti-dumping duties on Chinese/Korean imports.

open.item: Contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for stood at ` 65.60 Crores as at March 31, 2026, against which an advance of ` 27.97 Crores has been paid.
Withdrew/suspended the previously firm INR2,500 crores FY26 revenue guidance, declining to give any guidance due to US tariff uncertainty (last year did INR2,100 cr).
Aims to expand OEM brand dealership network from 500 to 900 dealers within the next two years.
Launched/scaling sustainable TPU-based UV printable films, PDLC (privacy-on-demand switchable) specialty films and advanced graphic solutions as next-phase high-value growth drivers.

US additional tariff now down to 10% (from 50%, off around 20 Feb 2026) over 6.26% base; anticipates a positive India antidumping-duty decision on China/Korea imports within a month or two; pursuing US tariff refunds (treated conservatively).
Garware Application Studios over 250 locations, on track to cross 300 shortly; added 11 new global application studios (UAE/US) during the year.
TPU line expected to be commissioned by October 2026; 25% capacity for new products with 2 identified (one automotive, one architectural) to begin sales from Q3FY27.
TPU line expected to deliver ~1.5-2% margin improvement at company level once operational.
TPU/backward integration expected to add ~1-1.5% (certain, per CFO; ~1.5-2% per MD) improvement to gross/operating margin once operational.
TPU line expected to deliver ~INR40-45 crores annualized savings flowing into EBITDA (33-month payback on INR118 cr).
Guides to a minimum INR2,500 crores revenue for FY27 (tariff now largely off), targeting ~20% CAGR resumption; new products (graphics, PDLC, printable PPF) on top of that.

Middle East/North Africa (MENA) sales ~$15 million; targeting $20-22 million this year (~25-30% CAGR); UAE subsidiary completed, with manufacturing/value-addition work underway for supply-chain flexibility.
Garware Home Solutions has 6 studios operational; targeting 50 GHS studios by end of FY27, and expects GHS plus new products (PDLC etc.) to cross INR200 crores by end of FY28 (~INR50 cr in FY27).
Tightened EBITDA margin guidance to 25% plus/minus 2% (from plus/minus 3%), with margin improvement expected once TPU line comes on stream.
Second PPF line to add ~INR400-450 crores revenue stepwise; peak revenue potential from existing capacity (full window-film + second PPF line utilization) estimated ~INR3,000 crores.
Expects domestic Sun Control Film business to contribute around 6% to 8% of total revenue in the next 3-4 years.
Announced INR191 crores new sun control film line (~1,200 lakh sq ft, ~30% capacity addition) with advanced robotics/automation; commercial production to start by June 2027 (Q1FY28).

currentContext.strategies: Expand and diversify the product portfolio toward specialty and novel products, led by the upcoming TPU product line|Shift mix further toward Value Added Products, repurposing older lines for specialty film production to lift capacity utilisation and make earnings more predictable|Diversify export markets away from US concentration — expansion into the Middle East via a planned Dubai subsidiary and a bolstered European team|Build B2C reach internationally through Global Application Studios in the United States and the Middle East|Launch a first-of-its-kind D2C business model in India through Garware Home Solutions, with strategic entry into the signage and digital printing segments|Broaden the automotive offering with advanced detailing products including ceramic and graphene solutions|Build direct digital channels (online sales, apps, digital marketing and channel-partner platforms) to enhance market access and brand loyalty|Digital transformation of operations: advanced analytics for manufacturing and supply chain, ERP upgradation, cybersecurity hardening and IT infrastructure enhancement|Sustain R&D-led differentiation through the DSIR-accredited R&D centre, launching coloured PPF, Headlight PPF, Spectrally Selective Films and Safety & Security Films|Operate an integrated Quality Management System spanning TQM, TPM, Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma, with external audits and independent evaluations
currentContext.expansion: GHFL is setting up a TPU plant with a capacity of 360 LSF per annum, which was under progress at the end of FY2025-26, and commissioned its second Paint Protection Film line in the second quarter of FY2025-26. The Board approved on January 22, 2026 the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai, UAE, still in process of incorporation, as part of a Middle East expansion that alongside a bolstered European team is intended to diversify export markets away from US geopolitical risk. The Company operates 3 manufacturing sites and 3 offices nationally plus 2 international offices (US and UK, for its subsidiaries), and runs four manufacturing lines housing administrative, manufacturing and R&D functions; it continues to repurpose older lines for specialty film production, which management describes as a key driver of strong capacity utilisation. Channel and footprint expansion includes the launch of Global Application Studios in the United States and the Middle East, over 250 Garware Application Studios, a D2C model through Garware Home Solutions in India, and strategic entry into signage and digital printing. Significant investments have been made in equipment modernisation to ensure operational efficiency and minimise disruptions.

risks.risk: Trade policy and tariff exposure on exports
risks.note: Management calls trade policy the most acute challenge: phased US tariffs on Indian exports of up to 50% were a major headwind in FY2026, and Q2 FY2026 revenues were down ~8% YoY due to the high tariff situation in the USA. Mitigation via cost efficiencies, front-loading shipments and market diversification, but the uncertainty remains.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility linked to crude oil
risks.note: The Company's major raw materials, PTA and MEG, are derived from crude oil, so crude price fluctuations directly impact raw material costs. Increases are passed on only to the extent feasible and required; commodity inflation in oil and energy also squeezed margins.

risks.risk: Currency fluctuation on a heavily export-weighted revenue base
risks.note: Given the Company's significant export revenues it is exposed to currency fluctuations. It appoints consultants who advise on global economic events and their impact on currencies, and hedges its net exposure through forward contracts.

risks.risk: Competition risk from capacity additions by global and domestic film majors
risks.note: The Company is sensitive to industry capacity, output levels, economic conditions and changes in consumer demand; the addition of capacities by competitors has intensified competition. Mitigated through product differentiation, market expansion and continuous market analysis.

Equipment obsolescence could disrupt production. The Company monitors equipment performance, conducts timely upgrades and preventive maintenance, and has made significant investments in equipment modernisation.

Logistics risks encompass transportation challenges and the availability of shipping containers, with geopolitical challenges from the Middle East and Eastern Europe; the Directors' Report also cites the impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict alongside U.S. tariff uncertainty.

risks.risk: End-market cyclicality and demand concentration in automotive and real estate
risks.note: In domestic markets, timely project execution such as new real-estate projects can be cyclical, and any slowdown in key end-user sectors (automotive, real estate) would impact volumes.

risks.risk: Broad enterprise risk set flagged by the Board
risks.note: The Company's ERM exercise identifies changing regulations, intensifying competition, business uncertainties, technological obsolescence, investment risks, financial challenges, environmental concerns and talent retention as key risks. The Board holds overall responsibility for the risk management framework, supported by a Risk Management Committee constituted under Regulation 21 of the Listing Regulations; in the Committee's and Board's opinion no risk threatens the existence of the Company.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GHFL manufactures BOPET polyester films and value-added specialty films at a fully integrated chips-to-film plant, producing its own resins in-house before converting them into finished film. Its portfolio spans architectural (sun control) films, automotive sun control and safety glazing films, paint protection films, and industrial/value-added films for electrical & electronics, packaging, thermal, shrink label and lidding applications. The business is organised into a Consumer Product Division serving solar control, window lamination, architectural and paint protection end-uses, and an Industrial Product Division supplying converters serving food, pharmaceutical and personal care brands.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Garware Home Solutions targeting INR200cr revenue by FY28; 50 D2C studios by FY27 end; Middle East subsidiary targeting $20-22mn (25-30% CAGR); TPU backward integration improving margins.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global push for energy efficiency and UV protection in buildings and vehicles underpins the Sun Control film business
- Growing luxury car and EV adoption supports the high-margin PPF segment
- Nascent 'smart glass' and architectural film markets offer high potential as commercial and residential developers seek modern solutions
- Trade policy is the most acute headwind — phased US tariffs on Indian exports of up to 50%, with Q2 FY2026 revenues down ~8% YoY on the tariff situation in the USA; mitigating actions taken were cost efficiencies, front-loading shipments and market diversification, but uncertainty remains
- Raw material volatility: PTA and MEG are crude-oil derived, so crude price moves feed directly into input costs; increases are passed on to the extent feasible
- Commodity inflation in oil and energy plus logistics costs squeezed margins
- Competitive pressure from global film majors continues, offset by GHFL's R&D and pricing flexibility
- Domestic project execution is cyclical, and a slowdown in key end-user sectors such as automotive and real estate would impact volumes
- Value Added Products reached 87% of total revenue in FY2025-26, reinforcing the transition toward high-value specialty businesses
- Despite uncertainty of U.S. tariff rates and the impact of the U.S.-Iran conflict, the Company was able to maintain profit levels broadly in line with the previous year

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: D2C margins 25-30% higher than B2B; Raw material (PTA/MEG) hikes largely passed through; 45-50% natural hedge on currency via import parity raw materials.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free balance sheet with INR774cr cash; All capex funded via internal accruals; Focus on high-ROI D2C infrastructure and capacity expansion.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: GHFL is setting up a TPU plant with a capacity of 360 LSF per annum, which was under progress at the end of FY2025-26, and commissioned its second Paint Protection Film line in the second quarter of FY2025-26. The Board approved on January 22, 2026 the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai, UAE, still in process of incorporation, as part of a Middle East expansion that alongside a bolstered European team is intended to diversify export markets away from US geopolitical risk. The Company operates 3 manufacturing sites and 3 offices nationally plus 2 international offices (US and UK, for its subsidiaries), and runs four manufacturing lines housing administrative, manufacturing and R&D functions; it continues to repurpose older lines for specialty film production, which management describes as a key driver of strong capacity utilisation. Channel and footprint expansion includes the launch of Global Application Studios in the United States and the Middle East, over 250 Garware Application Studios, a D2C model through Garware Home Solutions in India, and strategic entry into signage and digital printing. Significant investments have been made in equipment modernisation to ensure operational efficiency and minimise disruptions.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and aggressive on volume growth; Disciplined on capital allocation; Transparent on tariff headwinds; Bullish on D2C margin expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully vertically integrated chips-to-film production — complete control from petrochemical intermediate to finished product eliminates dependency on other manufacturers and gives high control over quality and product range
- India's only manufacturer of Sun Control films and Paint Protection Films, and the only producer of professional-grade PPF in India
- Specialised products carry significant entry barriers due to stringent quality focus, proprietary composition and processes, and limited competition
- Value Added Products accounted for 87% of total revenue in FY2025-26, making earnings more predictable and gross margins steadier as the mix shifts away from commodity
- ~90% market share in India's shrink film segment
- Distribution reach: 250+ Garware Application Studios, 90+ countries served, and a top-exporter position won from PLEXCONCIL for 38 consecutive years
- DSIR-accredited in-house R&D centre with pilot-scale plants, a pioneer in BOPET, solar control, lidding and PPF product development

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delay in US tariff refund accounting; Geopolitical disruption in Middle East shipping routes; Raw material volatility (PTA/MEG); Execution risk on 50-studio D2C rollout.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Sun-control line expansion prioritized over PPF due to higher fungibility (can produce PPF if needed) and larger absolute capacity addition (125 lakh sq ft/month vs 25 lakh for PPF); Architectural films growing faster than automotive due to 'privacy on demand' (PDLC) adoption.

margins & cost dynamics: D2C margins 25-30% higher than B2B; Raw material (PTA/MEG) hikes largely passed through; 45-50% natural hedge on currency via import parity raw materials.
capex / expansion: INR191cr for new automated sun-control line (new facility, operational Q1 FY28); Previous INR500cr+ spent on 2 PPF, 1 sun control, 1 metalizer, 1 TPU lines (fully funded by internal accruals).
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet with INR774cr cash; All capex funded via internal accruals; Focus on high-ROI D2C infrastructure and capacity expansion.
risks & watch-items: Delay in US tariff refund accounting; Geopolitical disruption in Middle East shipping routes; Raw material volatility (PTA/MEG); Execution risk on 50-studio D2C rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on volume growth; Disciplined on capital allocation; Transparent on tariff headwinds; Bullish on D2C margin expansion.
non-obvious takeaways: Sun-control line expansion prioritized over PPF due to higher fungibility (can produce PPF if needed) and larger absolute capacity addition (125 lakh sq ft/month vs 25 lakh for PPF); Architectural films growing faster than automotive due to 'privacy on demand' (PDLC) adoption.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
